title: Is Il San Pietro right for you?

turns.speaker: advisor
turns.text: Il San Pietro di Positano. Here's the thing to understand: you're not staying in Positano, you're staying on a cliff just outside it, and that's the whole point.

turns.speaker: traveler
turns.text: Which is either exactly what you want or a dealbreaker. Let's figure out which.

turns.speaker: advisor
turns.text: Every room has its own sea-view terrace. And there's an elevator carved into the rock that takes you down to a private beach, with a bar and a restaurant right on the water.

turns.speaker: advisor
turns.text: Very. Zass has a Michelin star, and the kitchens cook from the hotel's own garden terraces. Then every morning in season, their boats take guests out for a free cruise.

turns.speaker: traveler
turns.text: So, honeymooners. Couples who care about the table.

turns.speaker: advisor
turns.text: Exactly. Children only come from age ten, so it stays quiet.

turns.speaker: traveler
turns.text: A few things I'd tell a client. It's seasonal, roughly April to October. Town means hopping on the free shuttle. And the drive from Naples can crawl, so take their car-and-boat transfer.

turns.speaker: advisor
turns.text: Fair. If you want to wander Positano every night, that shuttle gets old.

turns.speaker: traveler
turns.text: Bottom line: book it to be away from the crowds, not in them. For a couple, it's the Amalfi Coast at its most private.

short_version.worth_knowing: Open roughly April–October; town is a shuttle ride away
